Implement the following plan:

# Plan: Fix All Another World VM Issues

## Context

The KN5000 port of the Another World VM has 20 issues identified in the code review (`docs/code-review-2026-02-09.md`). These range from bytecode desync bugs (unimplemented opcodes that don't consume their arguments) to logic errors (MOV/ADD writing to wrong addresses) to missing features (condJmp, video 0x40, drawLineP/Blend). The port currently only plays the intro cinematic linearly. After these fixes, the intro should run correctly with all branching logic, and the infrastructure will be ready for additional game parts when resources are added.

**File to modify:** `src/another_world_vm.asm` (single file, all VM code)

## Fixes (in implementation order)

### 1. Fix endianness on fetch_word calls

The AW bytecode is big-endian but TLCS-900 is little-endian. Some opcodes already byte-swap with `EX W, A` (0x04 CALL, 0x07 JMP, 0x08 setVect) but others don't.

**Add byte-swap to:**
- Opcode 0x00 (movConst) line 1136: `LD DE, (XIX)` → read into WA, `EX W, A`, move to DE
- Opcode 0x03 (addConst) line 1199: `LD WA, (XIX)` → add `EX W, A` after
- Opcode 0x09 (DJNZ) line 1298: `LDW BC, (XIX)` → read into WA, `EX W, A`, move to BC
- Opcode 0x0B (setPalette) line 1331: `LD WA, (XIX)` → add `EX W, A` after

### 2. Fix opcode 0x01 (MOV) - write to correct destination

Current bug: XIY points to src variable after reading, never recalculated for dst.

**Fix:** Read src value, then recalculate XIY for dst before writing:
```asm
; Read dstVariableId into stack, read srcVariableId, get src value,
; then recalculate XIY for dst and write
```

### 3. Fix opcode 0x02 (ADD) - actually add values

Current bug: identical to (broken) MOV code, never adds.

**Fix:** Read dst value, read src value, add them, write back to dst.

### 4. Implement opcode 0x0A (condJmp)

This is the most complex missing opcode. Variable-length encoding:
- `subopcode = fetch_byte()` - bits 0-2: comparison type, bit 6: 16-bit imm, bit 7: variable ref
- `v = fetch_byte()` - variable index for LHS
- `c = fetch_byte()` - either: literal byte, high byte of 16-bit literal (if bit 6), or variable index (if bit 7)
- Optional extra byte if bit 6 set (16-bit immediate low byte)
- 6 comparison modes: eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le
- `offset = fetch_word()` - jump target if condition is true

### 5. Implement opcode 0x0C (resetThread)

Consume 3 bytes (first, last, type). Freeze/unfreeze/delete thread ranges:
- type 0: freeze threads first..last
- type 1: unfreeze threads first..last
- type 2: delete threads first..last (set requested_PC = DELETE_THIS_THREAD)

### 6. Implement opcode 0x12 (drawString)

Consume 5 bytes (word stringId, byte x, byte y, byte color). Wire up to existing `DRAW_STRING` routine.

### 7. Implement opcode 0x13 (SUB)

Consume 2 bytes (dstVar, srcVar). `vm_var[dst] -= vm_var[src]`.

### 8. Implement opcode 0x14 (AND)

Consume 3 bytes (variableId, word value). `vm_var[id] &= value`.

### 9. Implement opcode 0x15 (OR)

Consume 3 bytes (variableId, word value). `vm_var[id] |= value`.

### 10. Implement opcode 0x16 (SHL)

Consume 3 bytes (variableId, word shiftAmount). `vm_var[id] <<= amount`.

### 11. Implement opcode 0x17 (SHR)

Consume 3 bytes (variableId, word shiftAmount). `vm_var[id] >>= amount`.

### 12. Implement opcode 0x40 (video with extended addressing)

Complex variable-length opcode. Following reference code:
- Read offset word, x byte
- Decode x based on opcode bits 5,4 (literal byte, 16-bit, variable, +0x100)
- Read y byte, decode based on bits 3,2
- Determine zoom from bits 1,0 (0x40 default, variable, fetch+discard, useVideo2)
- Call readAndDrawPolygon with computed parameters

### 13. Implement drawLineP

Read pixels from PAGE_BITMAP_0 at same Y,X coordinates and write to curPagePtr1.

### 14. Implement drawLineBlend

Read existing pixel from curPagePtr1, apply `(color & 7) | 8`, write back.

### 15. Implement opcode 0x0F (copyVideoPage) vscroll support

Add the `srcPageId & 0x80` conditional for vertical scroll using `VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y`.

### 16. Implement LOAD_SCREEN with screen_id dispatch

Use screen_id to select from available screen bitmap resources. Currently we only have resource-0x49 and resource-0x53, so map the known indices to available data.

### 17. Implement opcode 0x19 (LOAD) properly

The current stub skips the word but does nothing. Implement:
- `resourceId == 0`: no-op (would stop sound, but we don't have sound)
- `resourceId > 0x91`: set `REQUESTED_NEXT_PART` for level switching
- Otherwise: check screen_resource_indexes[] and call LOAD_SCREEN

### 18. Implement CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS part switching

Uncomment and implement the `m_requestedNextPart` check. Add `REQUESTED_NEXT_PART` variable. Implement `initForPart` which resets all threads and sets thread 0 PC=0.

Note: Full part switching requires bytecode/video/palette bank switching. We only have intro resources, so this will set up the infrastructure but log/ignore switches to unavailable parts.

### 19. Implement VM hacks

- `VM_HACK_INIT_VAR_54_WITH_81`: In GAME_RESET, set `vm_variable[0x54] = 0x0081`
- `VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED`: Initialize with a fixed seed (no RTC available)
- `VM_HACK_SWITCH_FROM_INTRO_TO_LAKE` and `VM_HACK_BLITFRAMEBUFFER_VAR_F7`: In opcode 0x10

### 20. INPUT_UPDATE_PLAYER stub

Add a proper stub that initializes the input-related VM variables to neutral values (no movement, no action). Full input via control panel serial requires significant additional work and will be a future enhancement.

## Verification

1. `make clean && make` - must build without errors
2. `make test` - run in MAME, verify intro cinematic plays correctly with polygon rendering
3. Check that the intro progresses through its sequence (thread scheduling, palette changes, polygon animations)

## Notes

- Sound opcodes (0x18, 0x1A) remain as consuming stubs - KN5000 sound hardware is not understood
- Only intro resources (part 1) are available; other parts need resource extraction
- Input requires control panel serial protocol implementation (future work)


If you need specific details from before exiting plan mode (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /home/fsanches/.claude/projects/-home-fsanches-devel-custom-kn5000-roms-anotherworld/203a1bcf-f5da-48ef-98cf-3f4ba7cc1ebc.jsonl

   648→readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy:
   649→	LD D, 0
   650→	LD E, C ; zoom
   651→	;	pt.x -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   652→	LD WA, 0
   653→	LD A, (XIX)
   654→	INC XIX
   655→	LD HL, (XSP + 6)
   656→	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.X *= ZOOM
   657→	SRA 6, WA			; PT.X /= default_zoom (40h)
   658→	SUB HL, WA
   659→	LD (XSP + 6), HL
   660→
   661→	;	pt.y -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   662→	LD WA, 0
   663→	LD A, (XIX)
   664→	INC XIX
   665→	LD HL, (XSP + 4)
   666→	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.Y *= ZOOM
   667→	SRA 6, WA			; PT.Y /= default_zoom (40h)
   668→	SUB HL, WA
   669→	LD (XSP + 4), HL
   670→
   671→	ld B, 0
   672→	LD C, (XIX)		; num_children - 1
   673→	INC XIX
   674→	INC BC			; BC = num_children

   676→children_loop:
   677→	LD WA, (XIX); offset 
   678→	INC 2, XIX
   679→	EX W, A
   680→	PUSH WA
   681→	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.x = pt.x
   682→	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.y = pt.y
   683→
   684→	; po.x += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   685→	LD WA, 0
   686→	LD A, (XIX)
   687→	INC XIX
   688→	LD HL, (XSP + 2)
   689→	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.X *= ZOOM
   690→	SRA 6, WA			; PO.X /= default_zoom (40h)
   691→	ADD HL, WA
   692→	LD (XSP + 2), HL
   693→	
   694→	; po.y += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   695→	LD WA, 0
   696→	LD A, (XIX)
   697→	INC XIX
   698→	LD HL, (XSP)
   699→	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.Y *= ZOOM
   700→	SRA 6, WA			; PO.Y /= default_zoom (40h)
   701→	ADD HL, WA
   702→	LD (XSP), HL
   703→
   704→	PUSH DE			; save zoom
   705→	LD DE, 0FFh				; uint16_t color = 0xFF;
   706→	LD HL, (XSP + 6) ;offset
   707→	AND HL, 8000h
   708→	JP Z, OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET
   709→	LD DE, 0
   710→	LD E,(XIX)				; 	color = m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] & 0x7F;
   711→	AND E, 7Fh
   712→	INC 2, XIX				; 	m_data_offset++; //and waste a byte...
   713→OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET:
   714→
   715→	PUSH XIX			;	 uint16_t backup = m_data_offset;
   716→	LD XIX, 0
   717→	LD IX, (XSP + 0Ah) ;offset
   718→	SLA 1, IX		 ; m_data_offset = (offset & 0x7FFF) * 2;
   719→	ADD XIX, INTRO_VIDEO_1
   720→	
   721→	LD HL, DE
   722→	; here L is the computer new color
   723→	; and BC is the children loop counter
   724→
   725→	; BC needs to become color | zoom params and
   726→	; DE needs to become x param
   727→	; to the readAndDrawPolygon routine
   728→	
   729→	LD DE, (XSP + 4)	; restore zoom
   730→
   731→	PUSH BC
   732→	LD B, L		; color
   733→	LD C, E		; zoom
   734→	LD DE, (XSP + 0ah)		; PO.x
   735→	LD HL, (XSP + 08h)		; PO.y
   736→	; (color, zoom, po)
   737→	CALL readAndDrawPolygon
   738→	POP BC
   739→	POP XIX				; m_data_offset = backup;
   740→	POP DE		; restore zoom
   741→
   742→	INC 6, XSP ; local vars offset, po.x, po.y
   743→	DJNZ BC, children_loop
   744→	RET

; (c) 2024 Felipe Correa da Silva Sanches <juca@members.fsf.org>
; Licensed under GPL version 2 or later.
;
; This is a port of the Another World VM (initially supporting only non-interactive
; playback of the game intro) to run from an extension board on a
; Technics SX-KN5000 musical keyboard.
;
; This program must replace the hd-ae5000_v2_01i.ic4 ROM of the extension board.
;
; This implementation is derived from my port of the Another World VM
; as a high-level emulation on MAME
;
; And that port was derived from Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM available at:
; https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
;
; The assembler I am using is compiled from source-code downloaded from
; http://john.ccac.rwth-aachen.de:8000/as/index.html
;
; Game assets must be extracted from an original copy of the game
; using the scripts provided at:
; https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
;
; === EQU Constants (shared) ===
PC_OFFSET			EQU 0  ; 16 bits
REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET	EQU 2  ; 16 bits
INACTIVE_THREAD		EQU 0FFFFh
DELETE_THIS_THREAD	EQU 0FFFEh
NO_REQUEST 			EQU 0FFFFh

CURRENT_STATE	EQU 0  ; boolean stored as a byte
REQUESTED_STATE	EQU 1  ; boolean stored as a byte

FROZEN	EQU 0
NOT_FROZEN EQU 1
NO_STATE_REQUEST EQU 0FFh

; These off-screen video pages are stored in external RAM:
PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 240000h
PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 250000h
PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 260000h
PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 270000h

CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN:
	; int16_t xmax = MAX(x1, x2);
	LD WA, (X1)
	CP WA, (X2)
	JP GT, XMAX_OK
	LD WA, (X2)
XMAX_OK:
	LD (LINE_XMAX), WA
	
	; int16_t xmin = MIN(x1, x2);
	LD WA, (X1)
	CP WA, (X2)
	JP LT, XMIN_OK
	LD WA, (X2)
XMIN_OK:
	LD (LINE_XMIN), WA
	RET

drawLineN:
	; Inputs:
	; C = color
	PUSH XIX
	PUSH XHL
	
	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN

	; for (int16_t x=xmin; x<=xmax; x++)
	; 	m_curPagePtr1->pix(m_hliney, x) = color;
	LD XIX, (CUR_LINE)
	ADDW (CUR_LINE_LOW), 320
	ADCW (CUR_LINE_HIGH), 0
	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
	EXTS XHL
	ADD XIX, XHL
	LD HL, (LINE_XMAX)
	SUB HL, (LINE_XMIN)

drawLineN_loop:
	LDB (XIX), C
	INC XIX
	DJNZ HL, drawLineN_loop
	
	POP XHL
	POP XIX
	RET

drawLineP:
	; TODO: Implement-me!
	jp drawLineN ; THIS IS INCORRECT!

	; Inputs:
	; C = color
	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN

	; for (int16_t x=xmin; x<=xmax; x++)
	; {
	; 	color = m_page_bitmaps[0].pix(m_hliney, x);
	; 	m_curPagePtr1->pix(m_hliney, x) = color;
	; }
	RET

drawLineBlend:
	; TODO: Implement-me!
	jp drawLineN ; THIS IS INCORRECT!

	; Inputs:
	; C = color
	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN

	; for (int16_t x=xmin; x<=xmax; x++)
	; {
	;	color = m_curPagePtr1->pix(m_hliney, x);
	;	m_curPagePtr1->pix(m_hliney, x) = (color & 0x7) | 0x8;
	; }
	RET

drawPoint:
	PUSH XIX
	LD WA, 0
	LD WA, HL
	MUL XWA, 320
	; FIXME: do we need to zero the upper 16 bits of XDE here?
	ADD XWA, XDE
	LD XIX, 01a0000h
	ADD XIX, XWA
	LD (XIX), BC
	POP XIX
	RET

video MACRO type,data,x,y
	LD XIX, INTRO_VIDEO_type
	ADD XIX, data
	LD DE, x
	LD HL, y
	LD BC, 0FF40h
	CALL readAndDrawPolygon
	ENDM


text MACRO stringid, x, y, color
	LD WA, stringid
	LD DE, x
	LD HL, y
	LD B, color
	CALL DRAW_STRING
	ENDM


BREAK:
	; This is a temporary placeholder
	; while we still do not emulate
	; the VM thread execution

	LD A, 0FEh		; end-of-frame
	CALL UPDATE_DISPLAY
	CALL PAUSE
	RET


UPDATE_DISPLAY:
	; A: PageID
	CP A, 0FEh
	JP EQ, _UPDATE_DISPLAY

	CP A, 0FFh
	JP EQ, _UPDATE_DISPLAY_PAGEID_FF

_UPDATE_DISPLAY_PAGEID_NOT_FE_OR_FF:
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2), XWA
	JP _UPDATE_DISPLAY
	
_UPDATE_DISPLAY_PAGEID_FF:
	LD XIY, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2)
	LD XWA, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_3)
	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2), XWA
	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_3), XIY

_UPDATE_DISPLAY:
	LD XHL, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2)
	LD XDE, 001a0000h + 20*320	; vga memory, skipping the first 20 lines because the image has 320x200 resolution and the screen has 320x240
	LD XBC, 320 * 200 / 2		; bitmap data length in 16-bit words (320x200 pixels)
	LDIRW
	RET


VIDEO_START:
	LD XIX, PAGE_BITMAP_2
	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_1), XIX
	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2), XIX
	LD XIX, PAGE_BITMAP_1
	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_3), XIX
	RET

GAME_RESET:
	CALL VIDEO_START
	LDB (CURRENT_THREAD), 0
	LDW (VM_PC), 0
	LD XIX, VM_STACK
	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIX
	
	; All threads are initially disabled and unfrozen
	LD IX, 0
_setup_threads__loop:

	PUSH IX
	SLA 2, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, THREADS_DATA
	LDW (XIX + PC_OFFSET), INACTIVE_THREAD
	LDW (XIX + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
	POP IX

	PUSH IX
	SLA 1, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
	LD (XIX + CURRENT_STATE), NOT_FROZEN 
	LD (XIX + REQUESTED_STATE), NO_STATE_REQUEST
	POP IX

	INC IX
	CP IX, 64
	JP NE, _setup_threads__loop
	
	; TODO: write_vm_variable(VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED, time(0) );
	
	RET

ENTRY:
	EI 06 ; DISABLE INTERRUPTS
	CALL GAME_RESET

MAIN_LOOP:

	CALL EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

	JP MAIN_LOOP

LONG_PAUSE:
	LD BC, 0
LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1:
	LD DE, 080h
LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2:
	DJNZ DE, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2
	DJNZ BC, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1
	RET

PAUSE:
	LD BC, 0
PAUSE_LOOP1:
	LD DE, 01h
PAUSE_LOOP2:
	DJNZ DE, PAUSE_LOOP2
	DJNZ BC, PAUSE_LOOP1
	RET

readAndDrawPolygon:
	; Inputs:
	; XIX: polygon data pointer
	; DE: x
	; HL: y
	; B: color (Black = FFh)
	; C: zoom (default = 40h)
	PUSH DE
	PUSH HL
	PUSH BC
	
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	CP A, 0C0H
	JP ULT, VALUE_IS_LT_C0

VALUE_IS_GTE_C0:

	CP B, 128
	JP ULT, COLOR_BIT_7_IS_OFF
	LD B, A
	ANDB B, 03Fh				;	if (color & 0x80) color = i & 0x3F;
COLOR_BIT_7_IS_OFF:
	
	;(&m_polygonData[m_data_offset], zoom);
	call readVertices

	; (color, pt)
	CALL fillPolygon

	JP end_of_readAndDrawPolygon

VALUE_IS_LT_C0: ; for now, here we simply assume value is == 2 without checking.
	;(zoom, pt)

	PUSH XIX
	PUSH BC ; C=zoom
	PUSH DE ; x
	PUSH HL ; y
	CALL readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy
	POP HL
	POP DE
	POP BC
	POP XIX

end_of_readAndDrawPolygon:
	POP BC
	POP HL
	POP DE
	RET

readVertices:
	PUSH XIX
	PUSH DE
	PUSH HL
	PUSH BC

	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	LD DE, 0
	LD E, C
	MUL XWA, DE			; *= ZOOM
	SRAW 6, WA			; /= default_zoom (40h)
	LD (POLYGON_BBOX_W), WA

	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	LD DE, 0
	LD E, C
	MUL XWA, DE			; *= ZOOM
	SRAW 6, WA			; /= default_zoom (40h)
	LD (POLYGON_BBOX_H), WA

	LD B, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	LD (POLYGON_NUM_POINTS), B

	LD XIY, POLYGON_POINTS
	LD DE, 0
	LD E, C

READ_THE_COORDINATES:

	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	MUL XWA, DE			; *= ZOOM
	SRAW 6, WA			; /= default_zoom (40h)
	LD (XIY), WA
	INC 2, XIY

	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	MUL XWA, DE			; *= ZOOM
	SRAW 6, WA			; /= default_zoom (40h)
	LD (XIY), WA
	INC 2, XIY

	DJNZ B, READ_THE_COORDINATES	

	POP BC
	POP HL
	POP DE
	POP XIX	
	RET

fillPolygon:
	; DE: x
	; HL: y
	; B: color (Black = FFh)

	PUSH BC
	LD C, B
	LD B, 0

	;if (m_polygon.bbox_w == 0 && m_polygon.bbox_h == 1 && m_polygon.numPoints == 4)
	CPW (POLYGON_BBOX_W), 0
	JP NZ, NOT_A_POINT
	CPW (POLYGON_BBOX_H), 1
	JP NZ, NOT_A_POINT
	CP (POLYGON_NUM_POINTS), 4
	JP NZ, NOT_A_POINT
	
	;(color, pt.x, pt.y);
	CALL drawPoint
	JP end_of_fillPolygon
	
	NOT_A_POINT:

	PUSH IX
	; int16_t xmin = pt.x - m_polygon.bbox_w / 2;
	LD IX, (POLYGON_BBOX_W)
	SRA 1, IX
	LD (POLYGON_XMIN), DE
	SUB (POLYGON_XMIN), IX

	; int16_t xmax = pt.x + m_polygon.bbox_w / 2;
	LD (POLYGON_XMAX), DE
	ADD (POLYGON_XMAX), IX

	; int16_t ymin = pt.y - m_polygon.bbox_h / 2;
	LD IX, (POLYGON_BBOX_H)
	SRA 1, IX
	LD (POLYGON_YMIN), HL
	SUB (POLYGON_YMIN), IX

	; int16_t ymax = pt.y + m_polygon.bbox_h / 2;	
	LD (POLYGON_YMAX), HL
	ADD (POLYGON_YMAX), IX
	POP IX


	;if (xmin >= 320 || xmax < 0 || ymin >= 200 || ymax < 0)
	;	return;
	CPW (POLYGON_XMIN), 320
	JP GE, end_of_fillPolygon
	CPW (POLYGON_XMAX), 0
	JP LT, end_of_fillPolygon
	CPW (POLYGON_YMIN), 200
	JP GE, end_of_fillPolygon
	CPW (POLYGON_YMAX), 0
	JP LT, end_of_fillPolygon


	LD WA, (POLYGON_YMIN)
	LD (HLINEY), WA

	LD XIX, POLYGON_POINTS				; i = 0;
	LD XIY, POLYGON_POINTS
	LD XWA, 0
	LD A, (POLYGON_NUM_POINTS)
	DEC A
	SLA 2, XWA
	ADD XIY, XWA						; j = m_polygon.numPoints - 1;

	; x2 = m_polygon.points[i].x + xmin;
	LD WA, (XIX)
	ADD WA, (POLYGON_XMIN)
	LD (X2), WA

	; x1 = m_polygon.points[j].x + xmin;
	LD WA, (XIY)
	ADD WA, (POLYGON_XMIN)
	LD (X1), WA

	INC 4, XIX		; 	i++;
	DEC 4, XIY		; 	j--;


	CP C, 10h
	JP Z, BLEND
	JP UGT, LINE_P

	LD XHL, drawLineN	; 	drawFct = &another_world_vm_state::drawLineN;
	JP AFTER_SETTING_DRAW_CALLBACK

	LINE_P:
	LD XHL, drawLineP	; 	drawFct = &another_world_vm_state::drawLineP;
	JP AFTER_SETTING_DRAW_CALLBACK

	BLEND:
	LD XHL, drawLineBlend

AFTER_SETTING_DRAW_CALLBACK:

	; uint32_t cpt1 = ((uint32_t) x1) << 16;
	LD WA, (X1)
	EXTS XWA
	SLA 16, XWA
	LD (CPT1), XWA

	; uint32_t cpt2 = ((uint32_t) x2) << 16;
	LD WA, (X2)
	EXTS XWA
	SLA 16, XWA
	LD (CPT2), XWA

POLYGON_RASTER_LOOP:
	DEC 2, (POLYGON_NUM_POINTS)

	CP (POLYGON_NUM_POINTS), 0
	JP Z, end_of_fillPolygon		; 	if (m_polygon.numPoints == 0) break;


	; 	int32_t step1 = calcStep(m_polygon.points[j + 1], m_polygon.points[j], h);
	PUSH XHL ; SAVE DRAW_FUNC_PTR
	PUSH XIX
	PUSH XIY
	
	; pt1 = j+1 / pt2 = j
	LD XIX, XIY
	INC 4, XIX
	LD XHL, STEP1
	CALL calcStep

	POP XIY
	POP XIX

	; 	int32_t step2 = calcStep(m_polygon.points[i - 1], m_polygon.points[i], h);
	PUSH XIX
	PUSH XIY

	; pt1 = i-1 / pt2 = i
	LD XIY, XIX
	DEC 4, XIX
	LD XHL, STEP2
	CALL calcStep

	LD XIX, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_1)
	LD XHL, 0
	LD HL, (HLINEY)
	MUL XHL, 320
	ADD XIX, XHL
	LD (CUR_LINE), XIX

	POP XIY
	POP XIX
	POP XHL ; RESTORE DRAW_FUNC_PTR

	INC 4, XIX		; 	i++;
	DEC 4, XIY		; 	j--;

	LDW (CPT1_LOW), 07FFFh		; 	cpt1 = (cpt1 & 0xFFFF0000) | 0x7FFF;
	LDW (CPT2_LOW), 08000h		; 	cpt2 = (cpt2 & 0xFFFF0000) | 0x8000;

	CPW (POLYGON_H), 0
	JP Z, POLYGON_H_IS_ZERO
	
FOR_H_LOOP:			; for (; h != 0; --h)
	CPW (HLINEY), 0
	JP LT, AFTER_DRAWFUNC_CALL

	LD WA, (CPT1_HIGH)		; x1 = cpt1 >> 16;
	LD (X1), WA

	LD WA, (CPT2_HIGH)		; x2 = cpt2 >> 16;
	LD (X2), WA


	; if (x1 < 320 && x2 >= 0)
	CPW (X1), 320
	JP GE, AFTER_DRAWFUNC_CALL
	CPW (X2), 0
	JP LT, AFTER_DRAWFUNC_CALL

	;	if (x1 < 0) x1 = 0;
	CPW (X1), 0
	JP GE, X1_NOT_NEGATIVE	
	LDW (X1), 0
X1_NOT_NEGATIVE:

	;   if (x2 > 319) x2 = 319;
	CPW (X2), 319
	JP LE, X2_LESS_THAN_SCREEN_W
	LDW (X2), 319
X2_LESS_THAN_SCREEN_W:
	
	;(x1, x2, color);
	CALL (XHL) ; drawfunc

AFTER_DRAWFUNC_CALL:
	
	LD WA, (STEP1_LOW)
	ADD (CPT1_LOW), WA
	LD WA, (STEP1_HIGH)
	ADC (CPT1_HIGH), WA	; 	cpt1 += step1;
	
	LD WA, (STEP2_LOW)
	ADD (CPT2_LOW), WA
	LD WA, (STEP2_HIGH)
	ADC (CPT2_HIGH), WA	; 	cpt2 += step2;

	INCW (HLINEY)
	CPW (HLINEY), 199
	JP UGT, POLYGON_RASTER_LOOP	; if (m_hliney > 199) return;

	DECW (POLYGON_H)
	JP NZ, FOR_H_LOOP

	JP POLYGON_RASTER_LOOP

POLYGON_H_IS_ZERO:
	LD WA, (STEP1_LOW)
	ADD (CPT1_LOW), WA
	LD WA, (STEP1_HIGH)
	ADC (CPT1_HIGH), WA	; 	cpt1 += step1;
	
	LD WA, (STEP2_LOW)
	ADD (CPT2_LOW), WA
	LD WA, (STEP2_HIGH)
	ADC (CPT2_HIGH), WA	; 	cpt2 += step2;

	JP POLYGON_RASTER_LOOP

end_of_fillPolygon:
	POP BC
	RET


calcStep:
	; Inputs:
	; XHL = ptr to STEP_1 or STEP_2
	; XIX = p1
	; XIY = p2

	PUSHW 4000h		; uint16_t v = 0x4000;

	LD WA, (XIY)
	LD (DX), WA		; dx = p2.x

	LD WA, (XIX)
	SUB (DX), WA		; dx -= p1.x;

	INC 2, XIX
	INC 2, XIY
	
	LD WA, (XIY)
	LD (POLYGON_H), WA		; dy = p2.y

	LD WA, (XIX)
	SUB (POLYGON_H), WA		; dy -= p1.y

	CPW (POLYGON_H), 0
	JP LE, POLYGON_H_IS_LE_ZERO  ; if (dy>0)
	
	LD WA, (XSP)
	EXTS XWA
	LD DE, (POLYGON_H)
	DIV XWA, DE
	LD (XSP), WA			; v = 0x4000/(POLYGON_H)

POLYGON_H_IS_LE_ZERO:
	
	LD WA, (DX)
	EXTS XWA

	LD DE, (XSP)		; v
	MULS XWA, DE
	SLA 2, XWA
	LD (XHL), XWA		; return dx * v * 4

	INC 2, XSP
	RET


readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy:
	LD D, 0
	LD E, C ; zoom
	;	pt.x -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	LD HL, (XSP + 6)
	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.X *= ZOOM
	SRA 6, WA			; PT.X /= default_zoom (40h)
	SUB HL, WA
	LD (XSP + 6), HL

	;	pt.y -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	LD HL, (XSP + 4)
	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.Y *= ZOOM
	SRA 6, WA			; PT.Y /= default_zoom (40h)
	SUB HL, WA
	LD (XSP + 4), HL

	ld B, 0
	LD C, (XIX)		; num_children - 1
	INC XIX
	INC BC			; BC = num_children

children_loop:
	LD WA, (XIX); offset 
	INC 2, XIX
	EX W, A
	PUSH WA
	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.x = pt.x
	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.y = pt.y

	; po.x += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	LD HL, (XSP + 2)
	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.X *= ZOOM
	SRA 6, WA			; PO.X /= default_zoom (40h)
	ADD HL, WA
	LD (XSP + 2), HL
	
	; po.y += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	LD HL, (XSP)
	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.Y *= ZOOM
	SRA 6, WA			; PO.Y /= default_zoom (40h)
	ADD HL, WA
	LD (XSP), HL

	PUSH DE			; save zoom
	LD DE, 0FFh				; uint16_t color = 0xFF;
	LD HL, (XSP + 6) ;offset
	AND HL, 8000h
	JP Z, OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET
	LD DE, 0
	LD E,(XIX)				; 	color = m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] & 0x7F;
	AND E, 7Fh
	INC 2, XIX				; 	m_data_offset++; //and waste a byte...
OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET:

	PUSH XIX			;	 uint16_t backup = m_data_offset;
	LD XIX, 0
	LD IX, (XSP + 0Ah) ;offset
	SLA 1, IX		 ; m_data_offset = (offset & 0x7FFF) * 2;
	ADD XIX, INTRO_VIDEO_1
	
	LD HL, DE
	; here L is the computer new color
	; and BC is the children loop counter

	; BC needs to become color | zoom params and
	; DE needs to become x param
	; to the readAndDrawPolygon routine
	
	LD DE, (XSP + 4)	; restore zoom

	PUSH BC
	LD B, L		; color
	LD C, E		; zoom
	LD DE, (XSP + 0ah)		; PO.x
	LD HL, (XSP + 08h)		; PO.y
	; (color, zoom, po)
	CALL readAndDrawPolygon
	POP BC
	POP XIX				; m_data_offset = backup;
	POP DE		; restore zoom

	INC 6, XSP ; local vars offset, po.x, po.y
	DJNZ BC, children_loop
	RET


LOAD_SCREEN:
; todo: ACTUALLY SELECT BITMAP VIA screen_id

	LD XDE, PAGE_BITMAP_0 + 20*320	; vga memory, skipping the first 20 lines because the image has 320x200 resolution and the screen has 320x240
	LD XBC, 320 * 200 / 2		; bitmap data length in 16-bit words (320x200 pixels)
	LDIRW
	RET

SETUP_PALETTE:
	; XWA: paletteID
	LD BC,0
	LD XDE, 01703c8h		; VGA 3c8 port (select color palette index
	LD (XDE), C

	LD BC, 2*16							; data length: 16 colors, 4 bits per component
	LD XDE, 01703c9h					; VGA 3c9 port (for setting the color palette values: r, g and b)
	LD XHL, INTRO_PALETTES
	SLA 5, XWA
	ADD XHL, XWA

PALETTE_LOOP:
	; red
	LD A, (XHL)
	ANDB A, 0Fh
	LD (XDE), A
	INC XHL

	; green
	LD A, (XHL)
	ANDB A, 0Fh
	LD (XDE), A

	; blue
	LD A, (XHL)
	SRA 4, A
	LD (XDE), A
	INC XHL

	DJNZ BC, PALETTE_LOOP
	RET


DRAW_STRING:
; WA: stringId
; DE: x
; HL: y
; B: color

	DEC DE
	SLA 3, DE 	;	x = 8 * (x-1);
	LDW (STRING_X0), DE	;	uint16_t x0 = x;
	LD XIX, STRING_INDEX
	EXTS XWA
	ADD XIX, XWA
	ADD XIX, XWA
	LD IX, (XIX)
	EXTS XIX
	ADD XIX, STRING_DATA
	LD C, (XIX)
	INC XIX

DRAW_STRING_LOOP:
	CP C, 0
	RET Z		;	for (; *c != '\0'; c++)

	CP C, 10	;		if (*c == '\n')
	JP NE, NOT_A_LINE_BREAK

LINE_BREAK:
	INC 8, HL			; y+=8;
	LD DE, (STRING_X0)	; x=x0;
	LD C, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	JP DRAW_STRING_LOOP

NOT_A_LINE_BREAK:
	CALL DRAW_CHAR
	INC 8, DE		; x+=8
	LD C, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	JP DRAW_STRING_LOOP


DRAW_CHAR:
	; DE: x
	; HL: y
	; B: color
	; C: character

	LD WA, 0
	LD A, C
	SUB A, 020h
	EXTS XWA
	SLA 3, XWA
	LD XIY, BITMAP_FONT
	ADD XIY, XWA

	PUSH XIX
	PUSH XHL
	PUSH BC

	EXTS XDE
	EXTS XHL

	LD XIX, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_1)
	MUL XHL, 320
	ADD XIX, XHL
	ADD XIX, XDE

	LD WA, 8
DRAW_CHAR_J_LOOP:
	LD C, (XIY)
	INC XIY			; uint8_t row = font[(character - ' ') * 8 + j];

	LD QWA, 8
DRAW_CHAR_I_LOOP:
	SLA 1, C
	JP NC, DONT_PLOT_THIS_PIXEL
	LD (XIX), B
DONT_PLOT_THIS_PIXEL:
	INC XIX
	DJNZ QWA, DRAW_CHAR_I_LOOP

	DEC 8, XIX
	ADD XIX, 320
	DJNZ WA, DRAW_CHAR_J_LOOP

	POP BC
	POP XHL
	POP XIX
	RET


GET_PAGE_PTR:
	; A: pageId

	CP A, 0FFh
	JP NE, PAGEID_NOT_FF
	LD XWA, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_3)
	RET

PAGEID_NOT_FF:
	CP A, 0FEh
	JP NE, PAGEID_NOT_FE
	LD XWA, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2)
	RET

PAGEID_NOT_FE:
	CP A, 3
	JP UGT, PAGEID_OTHER_VALUE
	AND WA, 3   ; 10000h bytes per page = enough for 320x200 pixels
	LD QWA, WA
	LD WA, 0
	ADD XWA, PAGE_BITMAP_0
	RET

PAGEID_OTHER_VALUE:
	LD XWA, PAGE_BITMAP_0
	RET


INPUT_UPDATE_PLAYER:
	; Implement-me!
	RET


CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS:

; TODO: Check if a part switch has been requested.
;	if (m_requestedNextPart != 0)
;	{
;		initForPart(m_requestedNextPart);
;		m_requestedNextPart = 0;
;	}

	LD A, 0
_check_thread_reqs__loop:

	; thread->state = thread->requested_state;
	PUSH WA
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
	LD E, (XWA + REQUESTED_STATE)
	CP E, NO_STATE_REQUEST
	JP EQ, _no_state_request
	LD (XWA + CURRENT_STATE), E
_no_state_request:
	POP WA

	PUSH WA
	SLA 2, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA
	LD DE, (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET)
	POP WA
	CP DE, NO_REQUEST
	JP EQ, _check_thread_reqs__next_loop

	PUSH WA
	SLA 2, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA
	LD BC, (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET)
	CP DE, DELETE_THIS_THREAD
	JP NE, _dont_delete_this_thread
	LD BC, INACTIVE_THREAD
_dont_delete_this_thread:
	LDW (XWA + PC_OFFSET), BC
	LDW (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
	POP WA

_check_thread_reqs__next_loop:
	INC A
	CP A, 64
	JP NE, _check_thread_reqs__loop

_end_of__check_thread_reqs:
	RET

.
NEXT_THREAD:
	CALL INPUT_UPDATE_PLAYER

	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (CURRENT_THREAD)

_next_thread__do_loop:
	INC A
	CP A, 64
	JP NE, _not_end_of_frame
	; == END OF FRAME ==
	LDB (CURRENT_THREAD), 0
	CALL CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS
	LD A, 0FEh
	CALL UPDATE_DISPLAY
	LD A, 0
_not_end_of_frame:

;	while(current->state == FROZEN || current->PC == INACTIVE_THREAD);
	PUSH WA
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
	LD E, (XWA + CURRENT_STATE)
	POP WA
	CP E, FROZEN
	JP EQ, _next_thread__do_loop

	PUSH WA
	SLA 2, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA
	LD DE, (XWA + PC_OFFSET)
	POP WA
	CP DE, INACTIVE_THREAD
	JP EQ, _next_thread__do_loop

_exit_do_loop:
	LD (CURRENT_THREAD), A
	SLA 2, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA
	LD DE, (XWA + PC_OFFSET) 	;	PC = current->PC;
	LD (VM_PC), DE
	RET


EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION:
	PUSH XIX
	PUSH XIY

	LD IX, (VM_PC)
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, INTRO_BYTECODE			; FIXME

FETCH_OPCODE:
	LD A, (XIX)  ; opcode = fetch_byte();
	INC XIX

	BIT 7, A	; if (opcode & 0x80)
	JP Z, OPCODE_BIT_7_NOT_SET

	; ====  VIDEO instruction (0x80) ====
_OPCODE_0x80:
;		uint16_t offset = ((opcode << 8) | fetch_byte()) * 2;
	LD W, A
	LD A, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	LD XIX, INTRO_VIDEO_1
	ADD XIX, XWA

	LD E, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	EXTZ DE		; x-coord
	
	LD B, (XIX)
	INC XIX
	EXTZ BC
	LD HL, BC	; y-coord

;		if (y > 199)
;		{
;			x += (y - 199);
;			y = 199;
;		}
	CP HL, 199
	JP UGE, _do_nothing
	ADD DE, HL
	SUB DE, 199
	ADD HL, 199
_do_nothing:

	LD BC, 0FF40h
	CALL readAndDrawPolygon

	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

OPCODE_BIT_7_NOT_SET:
	BIT 6, A	; if (opcode & 0x40)
	JP Z, OPCODE_BIT_6_NOT_SET

	; ====  VIDEO instruction (0x40) ====
_OPCODE_0x40:
;
;		int16_t x, y;
;		uint16_t offset = fetch_word() * 2;
;		x = fetch_byte();
;
;		m_useVideo2 = false;
;
;		if (!(opcode & 0x20))

;			if (!(opcode & 0x10))

;				x = read_vm_variable(x);
;		}
;		else
;		{
;		    if (opcode & 0x10)
;		        x += 0x100;
;		}
;
;		y = fetch_byte();
;
;		if (!(opcode & 8))
;		{
;			if (!(opcode & 4))
;				y = (y << 8) | fetch_byte();
;			else
;				y = read_vm_variable(y);
;		}
;
;		uint16_t zoom = 0x40;
;
;		switch (opcode & 0x03)
;		{
;			case 0:
;				zoom = 0x40;
;				break;
;			case 1:
;				zoom = read_vm_variable(fetch_byte());
;				break;
;			case 2:
;				fetch_byte();
;				break;
;			case 3:
;				m_useVideo2 = true;
;				zoom = 0x40;
;				break;
;		}
;
;		((another_world_vm_state*) owner())->setDataBuffer(m_useVideo2 ? VIDEO_2 : CINEMATIC, offset);
;		((another_world_vm_state*) owner())->readAndDrawPolygon(COLOR_BLACK, zoom, VMPoint(x, y));

	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

OPCODE_BIT_6_NOT_SET:


	; ====  MOV CONST instruction  ====
	CP A, 0
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_MOVCONST
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t variableId = fetch_byte();
	INC XIX
	LD DE, (XIX)	; int16_t value = fetch_word();
	INC 2, XIX
	LD XIY, VM_VARIABLES
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XIY, XWA
	LD (XIY), DE	; write_vm_variable(variableId, value);
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_MOVCONST:


	; ====  MOV instruction  ====
	CP A, 1
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_MOV
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t dstVariableId = fetch_byte();
	INC XIX
	PUSH WA
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t srcVariableId = fetch_byte();
	INC XIX
	LD XIY, VM_VARIABLES
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XIY, XWA
	LD DE, (XIY)	; value = read_vm_variable(srcVariableId);
	POP WA
	LD (XIY), DE	; write_vm_variable(dstVariableId, value);	
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_MOV:


	; ====  ADD instruction  ====
	CP A, 2
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_ADD
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t dstVariableId = fetch_byte();
	INC XIX
	PUSH WA
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t srcVariableId = fetch_byte();
	INC XIX
	LD XIY, VM_VARIABLES
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XIY, XWA
	LD DE, (XIY)	; value = read_vm_variable(srcVariableId);
	POP WA
	LD (XIY), DE	; write_vm_variable(dstVariableId, value);	
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_ADD:


	; ====  ADD CONST instruction  ====
	CP A, 3
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_ADD_CONST
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t variableId = fetch_byte();
	INC XIX
	LD XIY, VM_VARIABLES
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XIY, XWA
	LD WA, (XIX)	; int16_t value = fetch_byte();
	INC 2, XIX
	ADDW (XIY), WA	; vm_variable += value;	
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_ADD_CONST:


	; ====  CALL subroutine instruction  ====
	CP A, 4
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_CALL
	LD WA, (XIX)		; uint16_t address;
	EX W, A
	INC 2, XIX
	LD XIY, (VM_STACK_POINTER)
	LD DE, (VM_PC)
	INC 3, DE
	LD (XIY), DE		; push current program counter to VM stack
	INC 2, XIY
	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIY
	LD (VM_PC), WA
	JP _after_PC_update
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_CALL:


	; ====  RET instruction  ====
	CP A, 5
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_RET
	LD XIY, (VM_STACK_POINTER)
	DEC 2, XIY
	LD WA, (XIY)		; pop return address from VM stack
	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIY
	LD (VM_PC), WA
	JP _after_PC_update
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_RET:


	; ====  PAUSE_THREAD instruction  ====
	CP A, 6
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_PAUSE_THREAD
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (CURRENT_THREAD)
	SLA 2, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA

    LD DE, 0FFFFh ; HACK!!!!!!
	LD (XWA + PC_OFFSET), DE ; HACK!!!!!!

	LD DE, (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET)
	CP DE, NO_REQUEST
	JP NE, _pausethread_after_setting_request
	; When there's no other program counter request set
	; for this thread, we set the address of the
	; next instruction to resume execution
	; in the next VM frame.
	LD XDE, XIX
	SUB XDE, INTRO_BYTECODE		; FIXME
	LD (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), DE
_pausethread_after_setting_request:
	CALL NEXT_THREAD
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_PAUSE_THREAD:


	; ====  JUMP instruction  ====
	CP A, 7
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_JUMP
	LD WA, (XIX)	; word jump_address;
	EX W, A
	LD (VM_PC), WA
	JP _after_PC_update
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_JUMP:


	; ====  SET_VECT instruction  ====
	CP A, 8
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SET_VECT
	LD B, 0
	LD C, (XIX)	; byte thread_id
	INC XIX
	AND C, 3Fh	; (6 bits = max 64 threads);
	LD WA, (XIX)	; word request;
	EX W, A
	INC 2, XIX
	LD XIY, THREADS_DATA
	SLA 2, BC
	EXTZ XBC
	ADD XIY, XBC
	LD (XIY + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), WA
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SET_VECT:


	; ====  DJNZ instruction  ====
	CP A, 9
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_DJNZ
	ld WA, 0
	LD A, (XIX)	; byte variableId
	INC XIX
	LDW BC, (XIX)	; word address
	INC 2, XIX
	LD XIY, VM_VARIABLES
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XIY, XWA
	LD DE, (XIY)
	DEC DE
	LD (XIY), DE	; write_vm_variable(variableId, value);
	CP DE, 0
	JP Z, _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
	LD (VM_PC), BC
	JP _after_PC_update

INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_DJNZ:


	; ====  COND_JUMP instruction  ====
	CP A, 0Ah
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_COND_JUMP
	; Implement-me!
	INC 5, XIX ;
	;	uint8_t subopcode = fetch_byte();
	;	uint8_t v = fetch_byte();
	;	int16_t b = read_vm_variable(v);
	;	uint8_t c = fetch_byte();
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_COND_JUMP:


	; ====  SET_PALETTE instruction  ====
	CP A, 0Bh
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SET_PALETTE
	LD WA, (XIX)	; word paletteId
	SRA 8, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	CALL SETUP_PALETTE
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SET_PALETTE:


	; ====  RESET_THREAD instruction  ====
	CP A, 0Ch
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_RESET_THREAD
	; Implement-me!
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_RESET_THREAD:


	; ====  SELECT_VIDEO_PAGE instruction  ====
	CP A, 0Dh
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SELECT_VIDEO_PAGE
	LD A, (XIX)		; byte frameBufferId
	INC XIX
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_1), XWA
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SELECT_VIDEO_PAGE:


	; ====  FILL_VIDEO_PAGE instruction  ====
	CP A, 0Eh
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_FILL_VIDEO_PAGE
	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t pageId = fetch_byte();
	INC XIX
	LD B, (XIX)		; uint8_t color = fetch_byte();
	INC XIX
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD XDE, XWA
	LD A, B
	SLA 8, WA
	LD A, B
	LD BC, 320 * 200 / 2
_fill_videopage_loop:
	LD (XDE), WA
	INC 2, XDE
	DJNZ BC, _fill_videopage_loop
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_FILL_VIDEO_PAGE:


	; ====  COPY_VIDEO_PAGE instruction  ====
	CP A, 0Fh
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_COPY_VIDEO_PAGE
	;  FIXME: This is an incomplete implementation!
	LD A, (XIX)		; byte srcPageId
	INC XIX
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD XDE, XWA
	LD A, (XIX)		; byte DstPageId
	INC XIX
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD XHL, XWA
	LD BC, 320 * 200 / 4
_copy_videopage_loop:
	LD XWA, (XDE)
	LD (XHL), XWA
	INC 4, XDE
	INC 4, XHL
	DJNZ BC, _copy_videopage_loop
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_COPY_VIDEO_PAGE:


	; ====  BLIT_FRAMEBUFFER instruction  ====
	CP A, 10h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_BLIT_FRAMEBUFFER
	LD A, (XIX)		; byte pageId
	INC XIX
	CALL UPDATE_DISPLAY
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_BLIT_FRAMEBUFFER:


	; ====  KILL_THREAD instruction  ====
	CP A, 11h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_KILL_THREAD
	LD WA, 0
	LD A, (CURRENT_THREAD)
	SLA 2, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA
	LDW (XWA + PC_OFFSET), INACTIVE_THREAD
	CALL NEXT_THREAD
	JP _after_PC_update
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_KILL_THREAD:


	; ====  DRAW_STRING instruction  ====
	CP A, 12h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_DRAW_STRING
	; Implement-me!
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_DRAW_STRING:


	; ====  SUB instruction  ====
	CP A, 13h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SUB
	; Implement-me!
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SUB:


	; ====  AND instruction  ====
	CP A, 14h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_AND
	; Implement-me!
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_AND:


	; ====  OR instruction  ====
	CP A, 15h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_OR
	; Implement-me!
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_OR:


	; ====  SHL instruction  ====
	CP A, 16h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SHL
	; Implement-me!
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SHL:


	; ====  SHR instruction  ====
	CP A, 17h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SHR
	; Implement-me!
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_SHR:


	; ====  PLAY_SOUND instruction  ====
	CP A, 18h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_PLAY_SOUND
	; Implement-me!
	; Note: We currently do not understand the Technics KN5000 sound hardware.
	INC 5, XIX		; word resourceId; byte freq; byte vol; byte channel;	
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_PLAY_SOUND:


	; ====  LOAD instruction  ====
	CP A, 19h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_LOAD
	; Implement-me!
	INC 2, XIX		; word resourceId;
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_LOAD:


	; ====  PLAY_MUSIC instruction  ====
	CP A, 1Ah
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_PLAY_MUSIC
	; Implement-me!
	; Note: We currently do not understand the Technics KN5000 sound hardware.
	INC 5, XIX		; word resNum; word delay; byte pos;
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_PLAY_MUSIC:

		
_end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION:
	SUB XIX, INTRO_BYTECODE
	LD (VM_PC), IX
_after_PC_update:
	POP XIY
	POP XIX
	RET

1→# Code Review: KN5000 Another World VM Port
     2→
     3→## Comparison with reference MAME HLE implementation
     4→
     5→Reference commit: https://github.com/felipesanches/mame/commit/7cbb93bc3ee05f5ffdd083081530ac0daa2dfa84
     6→
     7→### Fully Implemented
     8→- **Opcode 0x00** (movConst) - OK
     9→- **Opcode 0x04** (CALL) - OK
    10→- **Opcode 0x05** (RET) - OK
    11→- **Opcode 0x06** (pauseThread/BREAK) - OK
    12→- **Opcode 0x07** (JMP) - OK
    13→- **Opcode 0x08** (setVect) - OK
    14→- **Opcode 0x09** (DJNZ) - OK
    15→- **Opcode 0x0B** (setPalette) - OK
    16→- **Opcode 0x0D** (selectVideoPage) - OK
    17→- **Opcode 0x0E** (fillVideoPage) - OK
    18→- **Opcode 0x10** (blitFramebuffer) - OK (missing pause-slices timing, but functional)
    19→- **Opcode 0x11** (killThread) - OK
    20→- **Opcode 0x80** (video instruction high bit) - OK
    21→- Polygon rendering pipeline (readVertices, fillPolygon, calcStep, readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy) - OK
    22→- Thread scheduler (NEXT_THREAD, CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS) - OK
    23→- Video page management (GET_PAGE_PTR, UPDATE_DISPLAY, VIDEO_START) - OK
    24→- Character/string drawing - OK
    25→
    26→---
    27→
    28→### Critical Missing/Broken Items
    29→
    30→#### 1. **Opcode 0x01 (MOV) - BUG: doesn't actually copy the value**
    31→(`another_world_vm.asm:1148-1165`)
    32→
    33→The MOV instruction reads `srcVariableId` and `dstVariableId` but the write at line 1163 writes to `XIY` which still points to `VM_VARIABLES + srcVariableId`, not `dstVariableId`. The `POP WA` on line 1162 restores dstVariableId, but XIY is never recalculated to point at it. The variable index in XWA is never used to recompute the destination address.
    34→
    35→#### 2. **Opcode 0x02 (ADD) - BUG: same as MOV, doesn't add**
    36→(`another_world_vm.asm:1168-1186`)
    37→
    38→This is literally a copy of MOV's code. It reads the source value but never adds it to the destination. It should: read dst value, read src value, add them, write back to dst.
    39→
    40→#### 3. **Opcode 0x03 (addConst) - Endianness bug**
    41→(`another_world_vm.asm:1189-1203`)
    42→
    43→The `fetch_word()` at line 1199 reads 2 bytes from the bytecode. But the reference uses big-endian reads (`READ_WORD_AW` = `READ_BYTE(A) << 8 | READ_BYTE(A+1)`), while `LD WA, (XIX)` reads in native little-endian order. The bytecode is big-endian (Amiga/68k origin). **This same endianness issue likely affects all `fetch_word()` operations throughout the code** (opcodes 0x00, 0x03, 0x04, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, etc.).
    44→
    45→#### 4. **Opcode 0x0A (condJmp) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    46→(`another_world_vm.asm:1316-1325`)
    47→
    48→This just skips 5 bytes and does nothing. The conditional jump is essential for all game logic (branches, comparisons). Without it, the game can only run linear sequences. The reference has 6 comparison modes (eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le) plus variable-length operands depending on subopcode bits 6-7.
    49→
    50→#### 5. **Opcode 0x0C (resetThread) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    51→(`another_world_vm.asm:1339-1344`)
    52→
    53→Doesn't even consume its 3 bytes of arguments (first, last, type). This will desynchronize the bytecode parser, causing every subsequent instruction to decode incorrectly. The reference implementation freezes/unfreezes/deletes ranges of threads.
    54→

# Code Review: KN5000 Another World VM Port

## Comparison with reference MAME HLE implementation

Reference commit: https://github.com/felipesanches/mame/commit/7cbb93bc3ee05f5ffdd083081530ac0daa2dfa84

### Fully Implemented
- **Opcode 0x00** (movConst) - OK
- **Opcode 0x04** (CALL) - OK
- **Opcode 0x05** (RET) - OK
- **Opcode 0x06** (pauseThread/BREAK) - OK
- **Opcode 0x07** (JMP) - OK
- **Opcode 0x08** (setVect) - OK
- **Opcode 0x09** (DJNZ) - OK
- **Opcode 0x0B** (setPalette) - OK
- **Opcode 0x0D** (selectVideoPage) - OK
- **Opcode 0x0E** (fillVideoPage) - OK
- **Opcode 0x10** (blitFramebuffer) - OK (missing pause-slices timing, but functional)
- **Opcode 0x11** (killThread) - OK
- **Opcode 0x80** (video instruction high bit) - OK
- Polygon rendering pipeline (readVertices, fillPolygon, calcStep, readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy) - OK
- Thread scheduler (NEXT_THREAD, CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS) - OK
- Video page management (GET_PAGE_PTR, UPDATE_DISPLAY, VIDEO_START) - OK
- Character/string drawing - OK

---

### Critical Missing/Broken Items

#### 1. **Opcode 0x01 (MOV) - BUG: doesn't actually copy the value**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1148-1165`)

The MOV instruction reads `srcVariableId` and `dstVariableId` but the write at line 1163 writes to `XIY` which still points to `VM_VARIABLES + srcVariableId`, not `dstVariableId`. The `POP WA` on line 1162 restores dstVariableId, but XIY is never recalculated to point at it. The variable index in XWA is never used to recompute the destination address.

#### 2. **Opcode 0x02 (ADD) - BUG: same as MOV, doesn't add**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1168-1186`)

This is literally a copy of MOV's code. It reads the source value but never adds it to the destination. It should: read dst value, read src value, add them, write back to dst.

#### 3. **Opcode 0x03 (addConst) - Endianness bug**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1189-1203`)

The `fetch_word()` at line 1199 reads 2 bytes from the bytecode. But the reference uses big-endian reads (`READ_WORD_AW` = `READ_BYTE(A) << 8 | READ_BYTE(A+1)`), while `LD WA, (XIX)` reads in native little-endian order. The bytecode is big-endian (Amiga/68k origin). **This same endianness issue likely affects all `fetch_word()` operations throughout the code** (opcodes 0x00, 0x03, 0x04, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, etc.).

#### 4. **Opcode 0x0A (condJmp) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1316-1325`)

This just skips 5 bytes and does nothing. The conditional jump is essential for all game logic (branches, comparisons). Without it, the game can only run linear sequences. The reference has 6 comparison modes (eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le) plus variable-length operands depending on subopcode bits 6-7.

#### 5. **Opcode 0x0C (resetThread) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1339-1344`)

Doesn't even consume its 3 bytes of arguments (first, last, type). This will desynchronize the bytecode parser, causing every subsequent instruction to decode incorrectly. The reference implementation freezes/unfreezes/deletes ranges of threads.

#### 6. **Opcode 0x0F (copyVideoPage) - Ignores vscroll parameter**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1379-1399`)

The reference reads `VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y` and supports vertical scrolling with source/dest Y offsets. The KN5000 version does a plain memcpy. Also ignores the conditional `srcPageId & 0x80` / `srcPageId & 0xBF` logic for special scroll behavior.

#### 7. **Opcode 0x12 (drawString) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1427-1431`)

Doesn't consume its 5 bytes of arguments (word stringId, byte x, byte y, byte color). Will desync the bytecode stream. The DRAW_STRING routine exists but is never called from here.

#### 8. **Opcode 0x13 (SUB) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1434-1439`)

Doesn't consume its 2 bytes. Will desync.

#### 9. **Opcode 0x14 (AND) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1442-1447`)

Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.

#### 10. **Opcode 0x15 (OR) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1450-1455`)

Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.

#### 11. **Opcode 0x16 (SHL) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1458-1463`)

Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.

#### 12. **Opcode 0x17 (SHR) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1466-1471`)

Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.

#### 13. **Opcode 0x19 (LOAD/updateMemList) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1484-1490`)

Skips the word argument but does nothing. In the reference, this handles:
- `resourceId == 0`: stop all sound
- `resourceId > 0x91`: switch to a new game part (level change)
- Otherwise: load a screen bitmap resource

#### 14. **Opcode 0x40 (video with extended addressing) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:1072-1125`)

The entire opcode 0x40 block is commented out and jumps to end without consuming any bytes. This handles polygon rendering with variable X/Y addressing modes and zoom. It's required for most in-game polygon graphics. **The variable-length encoding means skipping an unknown number of bytes, so this will definitely desync the VM.**

#### 15. **drawLineP - NOT IMPLEMENTED (falls through to drawLineN)**
(`another_world_vm.asm:89-102`)

Should copy pixels from page_bitmaps[0] to curPagePtr1, but just draws solid color.

#### 16. **drawLineBlend - NOT IMPLEMENTED (falls through to drawLineN)**
(`another_world_vm.asm:104-117`)

Should read the existing pixel and apply `(color & 7) | 8`, but just draws solid color.

#### 17. **INPUT_UPDATE_PLAYER - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
(`another_world_vm.asm:908-910`)

Returns immediately. Without input handling, the game can never be interactive. The reference reads button/keyboard state and sets ~8 VM variables for hero movement, action, and mask.

#### 18. **LOAD_SCREEN - Hardcoded to single bitmap**
(`another_world_vm.asm:747-753`)

Ignores the `screen_id` parameter entirely. The reference has 12 screen resources that get selected by index. Only one bitmap is ever loaded.

#### 19. **Part/level switching not implemented**
The reference has `initForPart()` / `setupPart()` which bank-switches bytecode, palettes, and video data when the game transitions between parts (intro, lake, jail, etc.). The KN5000 port hardcodes `INTRO_BYTECODE`, `INTRO_PALETTES`, `INTRO_VIDEO_1` labels, with no bank switching. `m_requestedNextPart` checking is commented out in `CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS`.

#### 20. **VM hacks not implemented**
The reference has several critical hacks:
- `VM_HACK_SWITCH_FROM_INTRO_TO_LAKE`: Sets var 0xDC when transitioning from intro
- `VM_HACK_INIT_VAR_54_WITH_81`: Required for the Interplay logo to show
- `VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED`: Never initialized (noted as TODO on line 228)

---

### Summary by Severity

**Will crash/desync the VM** (bytecode not consumed correctly):
- Opcode 0x0C (resetThread) - missing 3 bytes
- Opcode 0x12 (drawString) - missing 5 bytes
- Opcode 0x13 (SUB) - missing 2 bytes
- Opcode 0x14 (AND) - missing 3 bytes
- Opcode 0x15 (OR) - missing 3 bytes
- Opcode 0x16 (SHL) - missing 3 bytes
- Opcode 0x17 (SHR) - missing 3 bytes
- Opcode 0x40 (video extended) - variable length, unparsed
- Opcode 0x0A (condJmp) - skips 5 bytes, but actual length is variable (5-6 bytes depending on subopcode)

**Wrong behavior (logic bugs):**
- Opcode 0x01 (MOV) - writes to wrong variable
- Opcode 0x02 (ADD) - doesn't add, just copies (also to wrong dest)
- Big-endian fetch_word not handled (affects most word-reading opcodes)

**Missing but won't desync:**
- Input handling
- Part/level switching
- Sound (understandable given hardware constraints)

The port currently can only play the intro cinematic in a linear fashion (no branching, no interaction). To reach "complete and functional" status, the highest priority items would be: fixing the endianness issue, implementing condJmp (0x0A), fixing MOV/ADD, implementing the bytecode-consuming stubs to prevent desync, and then implementing opcode 0x40 for full polygon rendering.

1→# MAME Driver Source Files
     2→
     3→This directory contains a subset of MAME source files for the KN5000 driver. These are **reference copies** used for sketching driver improvements - NOT the complete MAME codebase.
     4→
     5→## Purpose
     6→
     7→These files serve as a workspace for:
     8→1. Planning control panel HLE (High Level Emulation) improvements
     9→2. Designing protocol implementations based on reverse engineering findings
    10→3. Drafting code changes before submitting to upstream MAME
    11→
    12→## Files
    13→
    14→| File | Description |
    15→|------|-------------|
    16→| `src/mame/matsushita/kn5000.cpp` | Main KN5000 driver - machine configuration, address maps, ROM definitions |
    17→| `src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.cpp` | Control panel HLE device implementation |
    18→| `src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.h` | Control panel HLE device header |
    19→
    20→## KN5000 Driver Architecture
    21→
    22→The MAME driver emulates:
    23→
    24→- **Main CPU**: TMP94C241F (TLCS-900/H2) at 20 MHz
    25→- **Sub CPU**: Second TMP94C241F
    26→- **Control Panel**: HLE device (no MCU ROM dumps available)
    27→- **Memory**: 16MB address space with ROM, RAM, and I/O regions
    28→- **Serial**: UART communication between main CPU and control panel
    29→
    30→### Control Panel HLE (`kn5000_cpanel_device`)
    31→
    32→The control panel uses High Level Emulation because the Mitsubishi M37471M2196S MCUs do not have ROM dumps available. The HLE device:
    33→
    34→- Implements serial communication via shift registers (RX and TX)
    35→- Uses a timer-driven baud rate generator (31,250 Hz default during init, 250 kHz normal operation)
    36→- Provides callbacks for TXD (transmit data) and SCLK (serial clock) signals
    37→- Sends initial command 0xE2 on startup (matches firmware expectations)
    38→
    39→### Communication Protocol
    40→
    41→The main CPU communicates with the control panel via serial at address `0x120000` (latch registers). The protocol uses:
    42→
    43→- **Commands**: E1, E2, E3, 00-1F (see control-panel-protocol.md in kn5000-docs)
    44→- **Responses**: Button states, encoder values, acknowledgments
    45→- **Packet types**: Single-byte, multi-byte, and special encoder packets
    46→
    47→## Workflow
    48→
    49→1. **Study**: Analyze reverse engineering findings from the disassembly
    50→2. **Design**: Draft improvements to HLE based on protocol understanding
    51→3. **Implement**: Update these reference files with proposed changes
    52→4. **Test**: Build MAME with the modified driver and test
    53→5. **Submit**: Create pull request to upstream MAME repository
    54→
    55→## Related Documentation
    56→
    57→- `../kn5000-docs/control-panel-protocol.md` - Complete protocol analysis
    58→- `../kn5000-docs/memory-map.md` - Hardware register addresses
    59→- `../maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.asm` - Main CPU disassembly (control panel routines at FC4xxx)
    60→
    61→## License
    62→
    63→These files are from MAME and are licensed under GPL-2.0-or-later. See individual file headers for copyright information.
    64→

1→; =============================================================================
     2→; main.asm - Another World VM for KN5000
     3→; =============================================================================
     4→; Unified platform wrapper for dual-target build:
     5→;   - TARGET_MAINCPU: Standalone main CPU ROM (0xE00000, for MAME testing)
     6→;   - TARGET_EXTENSION: HDAE5000 extension board ROM (0x280000)
     7→;
     8→; Build: make maincpu  OR  make extension
     9→;
    10→; Target: TMP94C241F (TLCS-900/H2) @ 25 MHz
    11→; =============================================================================
    12→
    13→	cpu 96c141		; TLCS-900/H target
    14→	page 0
    15→	maxmode on
    16→
    17→; =============================================================================
    18→; Include shared definitions from kn5000-roms-disasm
    19→; =============================================================================
    20→	include "sfr_tmp94c241.asm"
    21→	include "vga_constants.asm"
    22→	include "tmp94c241.inc"
    23→
    24→; Local macros not in the disasm repo
    25→	include "local_macros.inc"
    26→
    27→; =============================================================================
    28→; RAM Section (shared - both targets use external RAM at 0x200000)
    29→; =============================================================================
    30→	ORG 0200000h
    31→
    32→VM_VARIABLES:	DW	256 DUP (?)
    33→
    34→THREADS_DATA:	DW	64*2 DUP (?)  ; For each of the 64 threads:
    35→
    36→VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE:	DB	64*2 DUP (?)   ; For each of the 64 threads:
    37→
    38→CURRENT_THREAD: DB ?
    39→VM_PC:				DW ?
    40→VM_STACK_POINTER: DD ?
    41→VM_STACK: DW 256 DUP (?)
    42→
    43→POLYGON_NUM_POINTS:	DB ?
    44→POLYGON_BBOX_W:		DW ?					; uint16_t
    45→POLYGON_BBOX_H:		DW ?					; uint16_t
    46→POLYGON_POINTS:		DW	50 DUP (?, ?, ?)
    47→POLYGON_XMIN:	DW ?						; int16_t
    48→POLYGON_XMAX:	DW ?						; int16_t
    49→POLYGON_YMIN:	DW ?						; int16_t
    50→POLYGON_YMAX:	DW ?						; int16_t
    51→HLINEY:		DW ?							; int16_t
    52→CUR_LINE:			; uint32_t
    53→CUR_LINE_LOW:	DW ?
    54→CUR_LINE_HIGH:	DW ?
    55→
    56→CPT1:				; uint32_t
    57→CPT1_LOW:	DW ?
    58→CPT1_HIGH:	DW ?
    59→
    60→CPT2:				; uint32_t
    61→CPT2_LOW:	DW ?
    62→CPT2_HIGH:	DW ?
    63→
    64→STEP1:				; int32_t
    65→STEP1_LOW:	DW ?
    66→STEP1_HIGH:	DW ?
    67→
    68→STEP2:				; int32_t
    69→STEP2_LOW:	DW ?
    70→STEP2_HIGH:	DW ?
    71→
    72→; int16_t x1, x2;
    73→X1:			DW ?
    74→X2:			DW ?
    75→
    76→; 	uint16_t h;
    77→POLYGON_H:	DW ?
    78→DX:			DW ?	; int16_t
    79→
    80→;	int16_t xmax, xmin
    81→LINE_XMIN:	DW ?
    82→LINE_XMAX:	DW ?
    83→CUR_PAGE_PTR_1: DD ?
    84→CUR_PAGE_PTR_2: DD ?
    85→CUR_PAGE_PTR_3: DD ?
    86→
    87→STRING_X0: DW ?
    88→
    89→; =============================================================================
    90→; Main CPU ROM Layout
    91→; =============================================================================
    92→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
    93→
    94→STACK_TOP		EQU 001000h	; Stack in internal RAM
    95→OFFSCREEN_BUFFER_1	EQU 280000h	; Offscreen buffer (required by vga_init)
    96→
    97→	ORG 0E00000h
    98→
    99→; Fill with 0xFF until code section
   100→	rept 0F0000h		; ~960KB of padding
   101→	db 0FFh
   102→	endm
   103→
   104→	ORG 0EF0000h
   105→
   106→; Jump to Reset_Handler (VGA code is included first for macro definitions)
   107→	jp Reset_Handler
   108→
   109→; Include shared VGA I/O and initialization routines
   110→	include "vga_io.asm"
   111→	include "vga_init.asm"
   112→	ret			; VGA_Setup has no ret (designed for inline use)
   113→
   114→; Entry Point - Called after hardware reset
   115→Reset_Handler:
   116→	include "boot_hw_init.asm"
   117→
   118→	; Set up stack pointer (after hardware init)
   119→	LDA_XWA_IMM24 STACK_TOP
   120→	ld XSP, XWA
   121→
   122→	; Initialize VGA display using shared code
   123→	CALR VGA_Setup
   124→
   125→	; Turn screen on (sequencer clocking mode)
   126→	VGA_SEQUENCER 01h, 001h
   127→
   128→	jp ENTRY
   129→
   130→	endif ; TARGET_MAINCPU
   131→
   132→; =============================================================================
   133→; Extension Board ROM Layout
   134→; =============================================================================
   135→	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION
   136→
   137→	ORG 0280000h
   138→
   139→EXTENSION_HEADER:
   140→	db 'XAPR'
   141→	dd POINTERS
   142→	JP ENTRY
   143→POINTERS:
   144→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   145→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   146→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   147→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   148→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   149→
   150→	endif ; TARGET_EXTENSION
   151→
   152→; =============================================================================
   153→; VM Code (shared between both targets)
   154→; =============================================================================
   155→	include "another_world_vm.asm"
   156→
   157→; =============================================================================
   158→; ROM End (target-specific)
   159→; =============================================================================
   160→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
   161→
   162→Default_Handler:
   163→	halt
   164→	jr Default_Handler
   165→
   166→; Reset Handler Location
   167→	ORG 0FFFEE0h
   168→Reset_Entry:
   169→	jp Reset_Handler
   170→
   171→; Fill gap between reset entry and vector table
   172→	ORG 0FFFEE4h
   173→	rept 01Ch
   174→	db 0FFh
   175→	endm
   176→
   177→; Interrupt Vector Table
   178→	ORG 0FFFF00h
   179→VECTOR_TABLE:
   180→	dd 00FFFEE0h		; Vector 0: Reset
   181→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 1
   182→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 2
   183→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 3
   184→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 4
   185→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 5
   186→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 6
   187→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 7
   188→
   189→	rept 56
   190→	dd Default_Handler
   191→	endm
   192→
   193→	endif ; TARGET_MAINCPU
   194→
   195→	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION
   196→
   197→	ORG 02FFFFFh
   198→	db 0FFh
   199→
   200→	endif ; TARGET_EXTENSION
   201→
   202→; =============================================================================
   203→; End of ROM
   204→; =============================================================================
   205→	end
   206→

     4→; This is a port of the Another World VM (initially supporting only non-interactive
     5→; playback of the game intro) to run from an extension board on a
     6→; Technics SX-KN5000 musical keyboard.
     7→;
     8→; This program must replace the hd-ae5000_v2_01i.ic4 ROM of the extension board.
     9→;
    10→; This implementation is derived from my port of the Another World VM
    11→; as a high-level emulation on MAME
    12→;
    13→; And that port was derived from Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM available at:
    14→; https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
    15→;
    16→; The assembler I am using is compiled from source-code downloaded from
    17→; http://john.ccac.rwth-aachen.de:8000/as/index.html
    18→;
    19→; Game assets must be extracted from an original copy of the game
    20→; using the scripts provided at:
    21→; https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
    22→;
    23→; === EQU Constants (shared) ===
    24→PC_OFFSET			EQU 0  ; 16 bits
    25→REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET	EQU 2  ; 16 bits
    26→INACTIVE_THREAD		EQU 0FFFFh
    27→DELETE_THIS_THREAD	EQU 0FFFEh
    28→NO_REQUEST 			EQU 0FFFFh
    29→
    30→CURRENT_STATE	EQU 0  ; boolean stored as a byte
    31→REQUESTED_STATE	EQU 1  ; boolean stored as a byte
    32→
    33→FROZEN	EQU 0
    34→NOT_FROZEN EQU 1
    35→NO_STATE_REQUEST EQU 0FFh
    36→
    37→; These off-screen video pages are stored in external RAM:
    38→PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 240000h
    39→PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 250000h
    40→PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 260000h
    41→PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 270000h
    42→
    43→CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN:
    44→	; int16_t xmax = MAX(x1, x2);
    45→	LD WA, (X1)
    46→	CP WA, (X2)
    47→	JP GT, XMAX_OK
    48→	LD WA, (X2)
    49→XMAX_OK:
    50→	LD (LINE_XMAX), WA
    51→	
    52→	; int16_t xmin = MIN(x1, x2);
    53→	LD WA, (X1)
    54→	CP WA, (X2)
    55→	JP LT, XMIN_OK
    56→	LD WA, (X2)
    57→XMIN_OK:
    58→	LD (LINE_XMIN), WA
    59→	RET

    61→drawLineN:
    62→	; Inputs:
    63→	; C = color
    64→	PUSH XIX
    65→	PUSH XHL
    66→	
    67→	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN
    68→
    69→	; for (int16_t x=xmin; x<=xmax; x++)
    70→	; 	m_curPagePtr1->pix(m_hliney, x) = color;
    71→	LD XIX, (CUR_LINE)
    72→	ADDW (CUR_LINE_LOW), 320
    73→	ADCW (CUR_LINE_HIGH), 0
    74→	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
    75→	EXTS XHL
    76→	ADD XIX, XHL
    77→	LD HL, (LINE_XMAX)
    78→	SUB HL, (LINE_XMIN)
    79→

    81→	LDB (XIX), C
    82→	INC XIX
    83→	DJNZ HL, drawLineN_loop
    84→	
    85→	POP XHL

   119→drawPoint:
   120→	PUSH XIX

   153→	; while we still do not emulate
   154→	; the VM thread execution

   156→	LD A, 0FEh		; end-of-frame

   162→UPDATE_DISPLAY:
   163→	; A: PageID
   164→	CP A, 0FEh
   165→	JP EQ, _UPDATE_DISPLAY
   166→
   167→	CP A, 0FFh
   168→	JP EQ, _UPDATE_DISPLAY_PAGEID_FF
   169→
   170→_UPDATE_DISPLAY_PAGEID_NOT_FE_OR_FF:
   171→	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
   172→	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2), XWA

   175→_UPDATE_DISPLAY_PAGEID_FF:

   177→	LD XWA, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_3)
   178→	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2), XWA
   179→	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_3), XIY
   180→
   181→_UPDATE_DISPLAY:
   182→	LD XHL, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2)
   183→	LD XDE, 001a0000h + 20*320	; vga memory, skipping the first 20 lines because the image has 320x200 resolution and the screen has 320x240
   184→	LD XBC, 320 * 200 / 2		; bitmap data length in 16-bit words (320x200 pixels)

   188→
   189→VIDEO_START:
   190→	LD XIX, PAGE_BITMAP_2
   191→	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_1), XIX
   192→	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_2), XIX
   193→	LD XIX, PAGE_BITMAP_1
   194→	LD (CUR_PAGE_PTR_3), XIX

   196→
   197→GAME_RESET:
   198→	CALL VIDEO_START
   199→	LDB (CURRENT_THREAD), 0
   200→	LDW (VM_PC), 0
   201→	LD XIX, VM_STACK
   202→	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIX
   203→	
   204→	; All threads are initially disabled and unfrozen
   205→	LD IX, 0
   206→_setup_threads__loop:
   207→
   208→	PUSH IX
   209→	SLA 2, IX
   210→	EXTZ XIX
   211→	ADD XIX, THREADS_DATA
   212→	LDW (XIX + PC_OFFSET), INACTIVE_THREAD
   213→	LDW (XIX + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
   214→	POP IX
   215→
   216→	PUSH IX
   217→	SLA 1, IX
   218→	EXTZ XIX
   219→	ADD XIX, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
   220→	LD (XIX + CURRENT_STATE), NOT_FROZEN 
   221→	LD (XIX + REQUESTED_STATE), NO_STATE_REQUEST
   222→	POP IX
   223→
   224→	INC IX
   225→	CP IX, 64
   226→	JP NE, _setup_threads__loop
   227→	
   228→	; TODO: write_vm_variable(VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED, time(0) );
   229→	
   230→	RET

   232→ENTRY:
   233→	EI 06 ; DISABLE INTERRUPTS
   234→	CALL GAME_RESET
   235→
   236→MAIN_LOOP:
   237→
   238→	CALL EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
   239→
   240→	JP MAIN_LOOP
   241→
   242→LONG_PAUSE:
   243→	LD BC, 0
   244→LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1:
   245→	LD DE, 080h
   246→LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2:
   247→	DJNZ DE, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2
   248→	DJNZ BC, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1

   250→
   251→PAUSE:
   252→	LD BC, 0
   253→PAUSE_LOOP1:
   254→	LD DE, 01h
   255→PAUSE_LOOP2:
   256→	DJNZ DE, PAUSE_LOOP2
   257→	DJNZ BC, PAUSE_LOOP1
   258→	RET

   260→readAndDrawPolygon:
   261→	; Inputs:
   262→	; XIX: polygon data pointer
   263→	; DE: x
   264→	; HL: y
   265→	; B: color (Black = FFh)
   266→	; C: zoom (default = 40h)
   267→	PUSH DE
   268→	PUSH HL
   269→	PUSH BC
   270→	
   271→	LD A, (XIX)
   272→	INC XIX
   273→	CP A, 0C0H
   274→	JP ULT, VALUE_IS_LT_C0
   275→
   276→VALUE_IS_GTE_C0:
   277→
   278→	CP B, 128
   279→	JP ULT, COLOR_BIT_7_IS_OFF
   280→	LD B, A
   281→	ANDB B, 03Fh				;	if (color & 0x80) color = i & 0x3F;
   282→COLOR_BIT_7_IS_OFF:
   283→	
   284→	;(&m_polygonData[m_data_offset], zoom);
   285→	call readVertices
   286→
   287→	; (color, pt)
   288→	CALL fillPolygon
   289→
   290→	JP end_of_readAndDrawPolygon
   291→
   292→VALUE_IS_LT_C0: ; for now, here we simply assume value is == 2 without checking.
   293→	;(zoom, pt)
   294→
   295→	PUSH XIX
   296→	PUSH BC ; C=zoom
   297→	PUSH DE ; x
   298→	PUSH HL ; y
   299→	CALL readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy
   300→	POP HL
   301→	POP DE
   302→	POP BC
   303→	POP XIX
   304→
   305→end_of_readAndDrawPolygon:
   306→	POP BC
   307→	POP HL
   308→	POP DE

   311→readVertices:
   312→	PUSH XIX
   313→	PUSH DE
   314→	PUSH HL
   315→	PUSH BC
   316→
   317→	LD WA, 0
   318→	LD A, (XIX)
   319→	INC XIX
   320→	LD DE, 0
   321→	LD E, C
   322→	MUL XWA, DE			; *= ZOOM
   323→	SRAW 6, WA			; /= default_zoom (40h)
   324→	LD (POLYGON_BBOX_W), WA
   325→
   326→	LD WA, 0
   327→	LD A, (XIX)
   328→	INC XIX
   329→	LD DE, 0
   330→	LD E, C
   331→	MUL XWA, DE			; *= ZOOM
   332→	SRAW 6, WA			; /= default_zoom (40h)
   333→	LD (POLYGON_BBOX_H), WA
   334→
   335→	LD B, (XIX)
   336→	INC XIX
   337→	LD (POLYGON_NUM_POINTS), B
   338→
   339→	LD XIY, POLYGON_POINTS
   340→	LD DE, 0
   341→	LD E, C
   342→
   343→READ_THE_COORDINATES:
   344→
   345→	LD WA, 0
   346→	LD A, (XIX)
   347→	INC XIX
   348→	MUL XWA, DE			; *= ZOOM
   349→	SRAW 6, WA			; /= default_zoom (40h)
   350→	LD (XIY), WA
   351→	INC 2, XIY
   352→
   353→	LD WA, 0
   354→	LD A, (XIX)
   355→	INC XIX
   356→	MUL XWA, DE			; *= ZOOM
   357→	SRAW 6, WA			; /= default_zoom (40h)
   358→	LD (XIY), WA
   359→	INC 2, XIY
   360→
   361→	DJNZ B, READ_THE_COORDINATES	
   362→
   363→	POP BC
   364→	POP HL
   365→	POP DE
   366→	POP XIX	
   367→	RET

   369→fillPolygon:
   370→	; DE: x
   371→	; HL: y
   372→	; B: color (Black = FFh)
   373→
   374→	PUSH BC
   375→	LD C, B
   376→	LD B, 0
   377→
   378→	;if (m_polygon.bbox_w == 0 && m_polygon.bbox_h == 1 && m_polygon.numPoints == 4)
   379→	CPW (POLYGON_BBOX_W), 0

   381→	CPW (POLYGON_BBOX_H), 1

   386→	;(color, pt.x, pt.y);
   387→	CALL drawPoint

   389→	
   390→	NOT_A_POINT:
   391→
   392→	PUSH IX
   393→	; int16_t xmin = pt.x - m_polygon.bbox_w / 2;

   402→
   403→	; int16_t ymin = pt.y - m_polygon.bbox_h / 2;

   408→

   414→
   415→	;if (xmin >= 320 || xmax < 0 || ymin >= 200 || ymax < 0)
   416→	;	return;
   417→	CPW (POLYGON_XMIN), 320
   418→	JP GE, end_of_fillPolygon
   419→	CPW (POLYGON_XMAX), 0
   420→	JP LT, end_of_fillPolygon
   421→	CPW (POLYGON_YMIN), 200
   422→	JP GE, end_of_fillPolygon
   423→	CPW (POLYGON_YMAX), 0
   424→	JP LT, end_of_fillPolygon

   426→
   427→	LD WA, (POLYGON_YMIN)
   428→	LD (HLINEY), WA
   429→
   430→	LD XIX, POLYGON_POINTS				; i = 0;
   431→	LD XIY, POLYGON_POINTS
   432→	LD XWA, 0
   433→	LD A, (POLYGON_NUM_POINTS)

   452→	CP C, 10h
   453→	JP Z, BLEND
   454→	JP UGT, LINE_P
   455→
   456→	LD XHL, drawLineN	; 	drawFct = &another_world_vm_state::drawLineN;

   459→	LINE_P:

   463→	BLEND:

   466→AFTER_SETTING_DRAW_CALLBACK:
   467→
   468→	; uint32_t cpt1 = ((uint32_t) x1) << 16;
   469→	LD WA, (X1)
   470→	EXTS XWA
   471→	SLA 16, XWA
   472→	LD (CPT1), XWA
   473→
   474→	; uint32_t cpt2 = ((uint32_t) x2) << 16;
   475→	LD WA, (X2)
   476→	EXTS XWA
   477→	SLA 16, XWA
   478→	LD (CPT2), XWA

   480→POLYGON_RASTER_LOOP:

   482→
   483→	CP (POLYGON_NUM_POINTS), 0

   485→
   486→
   487→	; 	int32_t step1 = calcStep(m_polygon.points[j + 1], m_polygon.points[j], h);
   488→	PUSH XHL ; SAVE DRAW_FUNC_PTR
   489→	PUSH XIX
   490→	PUSH XIY
   491→	
   492→	; pt1 = j+1 / pt2 = j
   493→	LD XIX, XIY
   494→	INC 4, XIX
   495→	LD XHL, STEP1
   496→	CALL calcStep
   497→
   498→	POP XIY
   499→	POP XIX
   500→
   501→	; 	int32_t step2 = calcStep(m_polygon.points[i - 1], m_polygon.points[i], h);
   502→	PUSH XIX
   503→	PUSH XIY
   504→
   505→	; pt1 = i-1 / pt2 = i
   506→	LD XIY, XIX
   507→	DEC 4, XIX
   508→	LD XHL, STEP2
   509→	CALL calcStep
   510→
   511→	LD XIX, (CUR_PAGE_PTR_1)
   512→	LD XHL, 0
   513→	LD HL, (HLINEY)
   514→	MUL XHL, 320
   515→	ADD XIX, XHL
   516→	LD (CUR_LINE), XIX
   517→
   518→	POP XIY
   519→	POP XIX

   521→
   522→	INC 4, XIX		; 	i++;

   524→
   525→	LDW (CPT1_LOW), 07FFFh		; 	cpt1 = (cpt1 & 0xFFFF0000) | 0x7FFF;

   527→
   528→	CPW (POLYGON_H), 0

   533→	JP LT, AFTER_DRAWFUNC_CALL
   534→
   535→	LD WA, (CPT1_HIGH)		; x1 = cpt1 >> 16;
   536→	LD (X1), WA
   537→
   538→	LD WA, (CPT2_HIGH)		; x2 = cpt2 >> 16;
   539→	LD (X2), WA
   540→
   541→
   542→	; if (x1 < 320 && x2 >= 0)
   543→	CPW (X1), 320
   544→	JP GE, AFTER_DRAWFUNC_CALL
   545→	CPW (X2), 0
   546→	JP LT, AFTER_DRAWFUNC_CALL

   563→AFTER_DRAWFUNC_CALL:

   569→

   574→

   578→

   648→readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy:
   649→	LD D, 0
   650→	LD E, C ; zoom
   651→	;	pt.x -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   652→	LD WA, 0
   653→	LD A, (XIX)
   654→	INC XIX
   655→	LD HL, (XSP + 6)
   656→	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.X *= ZOOM
   657→	SRA 6, WA			; PT.X /= default_zoom (40h)
   658→	SUB HL, WA
   659→	LD (XSP + 6), HL
   660→
   661→	;	pt.y -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   662→	LD WA, 0
   663→	LD A, (XIX)
   664→	INC XIX
   665→	LD HL, (XSP + 4)
   666→	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.Y *= ZOOM
   667→	SRA 6, WA			; PT.Y /= default_zoom (40h)
   668→	SUB HL, WA
   669→	LD (XSP + 4), HL
   670→
   671→	ld B, 0
   672→	LD C, (XIX)		; num_children - 1
   673→	INC XIX
   674→	INC BC			; BC = num_children

   676→children_loop:
   677→	LD WA, (XIX); offset 
   678→	INC 2, XIX
   679→	EX W, A
   680→	PUSH WA
   681→	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.x = pt.x
   682→	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.y = pt.y
   683→
   684→	; po.x += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   685→	LD WA, 0
   686→	LD A, (XIX)
   687→	INC XIX
   688→	LD HL, (XSP + 2)
   689→	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.X *= ZOOM
   690→	SRA 6, WA			; PO.X /= default_zoom (40h)
   691→	ADD HL, WA
   692→	LD (XSP + 2), HL
   693→	
   694→	; po.y += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   695→	LD WA, 0
   696→	LD A, (XIX)
   697→	INC XIX
   698→	LD HL, (XSP)
   699→	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.Y *= ZOOM
   700→	SRA 6, WA			; PO.Y /= default_zoom (40h)
   701→	ADD HL, WA
   702→	LD (XSP), HL
   703→
   704→	PUSH DE			; save zoom
   705→	LD DE, 0FFh				; uint16_t color = 0xFF;
   706→	LD HL, (XSP + 6) ;offset
   707→	AND HL, 8000h
   708→	JP Z, OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET
   709→	LD DE, 0
   710→	LD E,(XIX)				; 	color = m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] & 0x7F;
   711→	AND E, 7Fh
   712→	INC 2, XIX				; 	m_data_offset++; //and waste a byte...
   713→OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET:
   714→
   715→	PUSH XIX			;	 uint16_t backup = m_data_offset;
   716→	LD XIX, 0
   717→	LD IX, (XSP + 0Ah) ;offset
   718→	SLA 1, IX		 ; m_data_offset = (offset & 0x7FFF) * 2;
   719→	ADD XIX, INTRO_VIDEO_1
   720→	
   721→	LD HL, DE
   722→	; here L is the computer new color
   723→	; and BC is the children loop counter
   724→
   725→	; BC needs to become color | zoom params and
   726→	; DE needs to become x param
   727→	; to the readAndDrawPolygon routine
   728→	
   729→	LD DE, (XSP + 4)	; restore zoom
   730→
   731→	PUSH BC
   732→	LD B, L		; color
   733→	LD C, E		; zoom
   734→	LD DE, (XSP + 0ah)		; PO.x
   735→	LD HL, (XSP + 08h)		; PO.y
   736→	; (color, zoom, po)
   737→	CALL readAndDrawPolygon
   738→	POP BC
   739→	POP XIX				; m_data_offset = backup;
   740→	POP DE		; restore zoom
   741→
   742→	INC 6, XSP ; local vars offset, po.x, po.y
   743→	DJNZ BC, children_loop
   744→	RET

content.content:
1→# Code Review: KN5000 Another World VM Port
     2→
     3→## Comparison with reference MAME HLE implementation
     4→
     5→Reference commit: https://github.com/felipesanches/mame/commit/7cbb93bc3ee05f5ffdd083081530ac0daa2dfa84
     6→
     7→### Fully Implemented
     8→- **Opcode 0x00** (movConst) - OK
     9→- **Opcode 0x04** (CALL) - OK
    10→- **Opcode 0x05** (RET) - OK
    11→- **Opcode 0x06** (pauseThread/BREAK) - OK
    12→- **Opcode 0x07** (JMP) - OK
    13→- **Opcode 0x08** (setVect) - OK
    14→- **Opcode 0x09** (DJNZ) - OK
    15→- **Opcode 0x0B** (setPalette) - OK
    16→- **Opcode 0x0D** (selectVideoPage) - OK
    17→- **Opcode 0x0E** (fillVideoPage) - OK
    18→- **Opcode 0x10** (blitFramebuffer) - OK (missing pause-slices timing, but functional)
    19→- **Opcode 0x11** (killThread) - OK
    20→- **Opcode 0x80** (video instruction high bit) - OK
    21→- Polygon rendering pipeline (readVertices, fillPolygon, calcStep, readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy) - OK
    22→- Thread scheduler (NEXT_THREAD, CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS) - OK
    23→- Video page management (GET_PAGE_PTR, UPDATE_DISPLAY, VIDEO_START) - OK
    24→- Character/string drawing - OK
    25→
    26→---
    27→
    28→### Critical Missing/Broken Items
    29→
    30→#### 1. **Opcode 0x01 (MOV) - BUG: doesn't actually copy the value**
    31→(`another_world_vm.asm:1148-1165`)
    32→
    33→The MOV instruction reads `srcVariableId` and `dstVariableId` but the write at line 1163 writes to `XIY` which still points to `VM_VARIABLES + srcVariableId`, not `dstVariableId`. The `POP WA` on line 1162 restores dstVariableId, but XIY is never recalculated to point at it. The variable index in XWA is never used to recompute the destination address.
    34→
    35→#### 2. **Opcode 0x02 (ADD) - BUG: same as MOV, doesn't add**
    36→(`another_world_vm.asm:1168-1186`)
    37→
    38→This is literally a copy of MOV's code. It reads the source value but never adds it to the destination. It should: read dst value, read src value, add them, write back to dst.
    39→
    40→#### 3. **Opcode 0x03 (addConst) - Endianness bug**
    41→(`another_world_vm.asm:1189-1203`)
    42→
    43→The `fetch_word()` at line 1199 reads 2 bytes from the bytecode. But the reference uses big-endian reads (`READ_WORD_AW` = `READ_BYTE(A) << 8 | READ_BYTE(A+1)`), while `LD WA, (XIX)` reads in native little-endian order. The bytecode is big-endian (Amiga/68k origin). **This same endianness issue likely affects all `fetch_word()` operations throughout the code** (opcodes 0x00, 0x03, 0x04, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, etc.).
    44→
    45→#### 4. **Opcode 0x0A (condJmp) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    46→(`another_world_vm.asm:1316-1325`)
    47→
    48→This just skips 5 bytes and does nothing. The conditional jump is essential for all game logic (branches, comparisons). Without it, the game can only run linear sequences. The reference has 6 comparison modes (eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le) plus variable-length operands depending on subopcode bits 6-7.
    49→
    50→#### 5. **Opcode 0x0C (resetThread) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    51→(`another_world_vm.asm:1339-1344`)
    52→
    53→Doesn't even consume its 3 bytes of arguments (first, last, type). This will desynchronize the bytecode parser, causing every subsequent instruction to decode incorrectly. The reference implementation freezes/unfreezes/deletes ranges of threads.
    54→
    55→#### 6. **Opcode 0x0F (copyVideoPage) - Ignores vscroll parameter**
    56→(`another_world_vm.asm:1379-1399`)
    57→
    58→The reference reads `VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y` and supports vertical scrolling with source/dest Y offsets. The KN5000 version does a plain memcpy. Also ignores the conditional `srcPageId & 0x80` / `srcPageId & 0xBF` logic for special scroll behavior.
    59→
    60→#### 7. **Opcode 0x12 (drawString) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    61→(`another_world_vm.asm:1427-1431`)
    62→
    63→Doesn't consume its 5 bytes of arguments (word stringId, byte x, byte y, byte color). Will desync the bytecode stream. The DRAW_STRING routine exists but is never called from here.
    64→
    65→#### 8. **Opcode 0x13 (SUB) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    66→(`another_world_vm.asm:1434-1439`)
    67→
    68→Doesn't consume its 2 bytes. Will desync.
    69→
    70→#### 9. **Opcode 0x14 (AND) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    71→(`another_world_vm.asm:1442-1447`)
    72→
    73→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    74→
    75→#### 10. **Opcode 0x15 (OR) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    76→(`another_world_vm.asm:1450-1455`)
    77→
    78→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    79→
    80→#### 11. **Opcode 0x16 (SHL) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    81→(`another_world_vm.asm:1458-1463`)
    82→
    83→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    84→
    85→#### 12. **Opcode 0x17 (SHR) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    86→(`another_world_vm.asm:1466-1471`)
    87→
    88→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    89→
    90→#### 13. **Opcode 0x19 (LOAD/updateMemList) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    91→(`another_world_vm.asm:1484-1490`)
    92→
    93→Skips the word argument but does nothing. In the reference, this handles:
    94→- `resourceId == 0`: stop all sound
    95→- `resourceId > 0x91`: switch to a new game part (level change)
    96→- Otherwise: load a screen bitmap resource
    97→
    98→#### 14. **Opcode 0x40 (video with extended addressing) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    99→(`another_world_vm.asm:1072-1125`)
   100→
   101→The entire opcode 0x40 block is commented out and jumps to end without consuming any bytes. This handles polygon rendering with variable X/Y addressing modes and zoom. It's required for most in-game polygon graphics. **The variable-length encoding means skipping an unknown number of bytes, so this will definitely desync the VM.**
   102→
   103→#### 15. **drawLineP - NOT IMPLEMENTED (falls through to drawLineN)**
   104→(`another_world_vm.asm:89-102`)
   105→
   106→Should copy pixels from page_bitmaps[0] to curPagePtr1, but just draws solid color.
   107→
   108→#### 16. **drawLineBlend - NOT IMPLEMENTED (falls through to drawLineN)**
   109→(`another_world_vm.asm:104-117`)
   110→
   111→Should read the existing pixel and apply `(color & 7) | 8`, but just draws solid color.
   112→
   113→#### 17. **INPUT_UPDATE_PLAYER - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
   114→(`another_world_vm.asm:908-910`)
   115→
   116→Returns immediately. Without input handling, the game can never be interactive. The reference reads button/keyboard state and sets ~8 VM variables for hero movement, action, and mask.
   117→
   118→#### 18. **LOAD_SCREEN - Hardcoded to single bitmap**
   119→(`another_world_vm.asm:747-753`)
   120→
   121→Ignores the `screen_id` parameter entirely. The reference has 12 screen resources that get selected by index. Only one bitmap is ever loaded.
   122→
   123→#### 19. **Part/level switching not implemented**
   124→The reference has `initForPart()` / `setupPart()` which bank-switches bytecode, palettes, and video data when the game transitions between parts (intro, lake, jail, etc.). The KN5000 port hardcodes `INTRO_BYTECODE`, `INTRO_PALETTES`, `INTRO_VIDEO_1` labels, with no bank switching. `m_requestedNextPart` checking is commented out in `CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS`.
   125→
   126→#### 20. **VM hacks not implemented**
   127→The reference has several critical hacks:
   128→- `VM_HACK_SWITCH_FROM_INTRO_TO_LAKE`: Sets var 0xDC when transitioning from intro
   129→- `VM_HACK_INIT_VAR_54_WITH_81`: Required for the Interplay logo to show
   130→- `VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED`: Never initialized (noted as TODO on line 228)
   131→
   132→---
   133→
   134→### Summary by Severity
   135→
   136→**Will crash/desync the VM** (bytecode not consumed correctly):
   137→- Opcode 0x0C (resetThread) - missing 3 bytes
   138→- Opcode 0x12 (drawString) - missing 5 bytes
   139→- Opcode 0x13 (SUB) - missing 2 bytes
   140→- Opcode 0x14 (AND) - missing 3 bytes
   141→- Opcode 0x15 (OR) - missing 3 bytes
   142→- Opcode 0x16 (SHL) - missing 3 bytes
   143→- Opcode 0x17 (SHR) - missing 3 bytes
   144→- Opcode 0x40 (video extended) - variable length, unparsed
   145→- Opcode 0x0A (condJmp) - skips 5 bytes, but actual length is variable (5-6 bytes depending on subopcode)
   146→
   147→**Wrong behavior (logic bugs):**
   148→- Opcode 0x01 (MOV) - writes to wrong variable
   149→- Opcode 0x02 (ADD) - doesn't add, just copies (also to wrong dest)
   150→- Big-endian fetch_word not handled (affects most word-reading opcodes)
   151→
   152→**Missing but won't desync:**
   153→- Input handling
   154→- Part/level switching
   155→- Sound (understandable given hardware constraints)
   156→
   157→The port currently can only play the intro cinematic in a linear fashion (no branching, no interaction). To reach "complete and functional" status, the highest priority items would be: fixing the endianness issue, implementing condJmp (0x0A), fixing MOV/ADD, implementing the bytecode-consuming stubs to prevent desync, and then implementing opcode 0x40 for full polygon rendering.
